claim: The bowl gives about 60 G at the 100 mm reference radius at 730 rpm
law: Centripetal acceleration a = omega^2 r

claim: Fine gold reaches the bowl wall before it leaves: a 20 um gold flake crosses the 5 mm film well within the transit time
law: Terminal velocity in the centrifugal field with Schiller and Naumann drag; flake at half the sphere velocity

claim: The fluidized bed in the riffle rings keeps fine gold (80 % of 75 to 1,000 um, 50 % of 38 to 75 um; about 71 % of screened gold) while the bed is flushed every 2 h
law: Fluidized centrifugal concentrators recover very fine gold over a wide size range (Veiga and Gunson 2020). The 2.7 mm/s upflow is about the minimum fluidization velocity of 75 um quartz at 60 G (2.9 mm/s, Wen and Yu) and well below that of coarser or denser grains (27 mm/s for 150 um pyrite), so most of the bed is not fully fluidized; commercial bowls use 10 to 30 L/min at 35 to 100 kPa (iCON i150) against 12 L/min at about 10 kPa here; saturation by heavy minerals in the feed is not calculable
check: Settling check passes (S2); retention needs a test with characterized or spiked ore (PR-004, TRL 4)

claim: The 1.7 m header post gives the proposed 10 kPa net at every ring at 600 rpm with the tank half full, without a pump
law: Static head less hose, fittings and filter losses (Darcy-Weisbach, K factors), less the climb from the union to the ring (rho g dz), plus rho omega^2 r^2 / 2 in the jacket. v0.8 left out the climb (4.5 to 5.6 kPa) and had 6.0 kPa: fixed by 3/4 in valve and rotameter

claim: Water still enters every ring with the tank nearly empty and the filter at its cleaning point
law: Lowest net ring pressure at 600 rpm, tank 50 mm above its floor, filter K 6

claim: Bringing the slurry and water to lip speed takes about 27 W at 730 rpm
law: Power = m v^2 at the lip: half leaves as kinetic energy, half is lost in slip in the film (an upper bound); bowl and table never run together

claim: Bowl, jacket and rings keep a burst safety factor of at least 10 at 1,200 rpm (a sprinting rider)
law: Thin-wall hoop stress from jacket water pressure and self-weight; GFRP 80 MPa, PU 20 MPa (typical)

claim: The spindle's first critical speed is well above the highest reachable bowl speed (1.25 x 1,200 rpm)
law: Cantilever 3EI/L^3 of the 25 x 2 mm tube gives 2710 rpm on rigid bearings; with the compliance of the 25 x 25 x 1.5 members the bearings hang from, magnified by the 210 mm overhang over the 165 mm bearing span, 1274 rpm (member ends pinned) to 1976 rpm (fixed)
check: Above 900 rpm, the limit, in every case; against 1,500 rpm only if the members act nearly fixed. Tap test on the first frame at TRL 4 (GVS-DEC-001 O4)

claim: The disc brake stops the bowl within the 15 s of PR-012
law: t = I omega / (T_brake + T_drag); bicycle disc, mu 0.4, 150 N per pad at 70 mm

claim: The 6 mm HDPE tub and 10 mm lid contain a fragment of the bowl thrown off at 900 to 1,200 rpm
law: Oblique impact: normal share 0.66 of 61 J gives 40 J at 1,200 rpm and 22 J at 900 rpm into the wall; plugging energy of the wall 57 J face first, 14 J edge first (dishing not counted); a quarter of the whole bowl group (review's bounding case) puts 125 J into the wall
check: Not shown edge first, nor for the bounding case. Fix proposed: a 3 mm steel band (it breaks PR-011, so it goes to Amish, GVS-DEC-001 O2), or an impact test before any spin test

claim: With a full tank the machine stands on a 10 degree slope in any direction
law: Tipping about the narrowest base (600 mm) with the frame-borne mass at 0.55 m and a full 64 kg tank on the post

claim: The spindle members carry the belt pull, rotor weight and unbalance with a safety factor of at least 1.5 on yield
law: Central point load on a pinned 600 mm span of 25 x 25 x 1.5 tube, S235

claim: The tank post above the braces does not yield at the side push that tips the machine
law: Cantilever bending of 25 x 25 x 1.5 tube above the brace node

claim: The rubber bump stop makes the table stroke asymmetric: the deck stops sharply at the far end and turns smoothly at the head end
law: Impact of the 17 kg deck on a bonded rubber buffer (shape factor), against the harmonic turn at the head end

claim: The shaking table reduces about 5.3 kg of bowl concentrate to 100 g or less in two passes (53:1)
law: Shaking tables reach concentration ratios of 28.8 to 170.9 (mean 66.7) at the MICA plant in Migori, Kenya (Mitchell et al. 2026); a 1,000 x 450 mm table on a heavy-mineral concentrate is not proven
check: Two passes at 8:1 give 64:1 on paper (PR-005 at risk); test at TRL 4

claim: The bump stop buffer works within its rating at the largest setting
law: Peak buffer force at the 6 mm setting against the buffer's rated compression load (the BOM said 600 N; now 800 N, as GVS-CAL-001 section 9 chose)

claim: A 61 rpm cadence turns the bowl at about 730 rpm through 48T/12T, 1:1 and 300/100
law: Product of the stage ratios

claim: A bicycle computer set to 1,667 mm reads bowl rpm divided by 10
law: Speed = rpm x wheel size x 60 / 1000
check: claimed 73 km/h at 730 rpm, estimate 73 km/h at 730 rpm (ratio 1.00)

claim: Water use is 1.19 m3/h: slurry water at 30 % solids plus 12 L/min of fluidization
law: Mass balance of water

claim: The 60 L header drum holds 60 L as drawn
law: Volume of the drawn drum (was 400 mm tall: 45 L)

claim: The gold balance is consistent: 7.75 g in per shift on 5 g/t ore (1.55 t of feed), about 60 % smelted as the product of the assumed stage recoveries (the recoveries themselves are S3 and S15)
law: Product of assumed stage recoveries (0.602); gold in = grade x feed time (was the full 8 h: 8.0 g)

claim: Each flush yields about 1.33 kg of concentrate, a mass pull of 0.33 %
law: Groove volume x 60 % fill x 2.5 kg/L wet bulk

claim: With the motor the bowl cannot exceed 900 rpm
law: The 1.2:1 step-up is chosen from an assumed 250 rpm no-load motor speed (no datasheet), so the kinematic cap holds only if the motor's real no-load speed at full pack voltage is 250 rpm or less; MotionCore's own speed limit is the second cap
check: To confirm against the motor datasheet when bought (GVS-DEC-001, to confirm item 10)

claim: The fluidization water is clean enough for 1.0 mm holes: a screen filter stops grains that could block them
law: Fluidization water must be clean (Veiga and Gunson 2020). The 120 mesh screen stops grains over 0.125 mm, an eighth of the hole size; silt finer than that and biofilm still pass, and the right ratio for silty pond water is not sourced here
check: Flow through every ring after the filter to check at TRL 4 (BLD first checks)

claim: A local workshop builds every part without a lathe; the liner is cast in a printed mold
law: Set-screw insert bearings, a taper bush and a welded nipple avoid turning (GVS-DDR-003); casting a Shore 85A PU liner on a six-segment printed core is common practice in PU shops but untried here
check: Casting route to try at TRL 4 (PR-010)

claim: A rider supplies 48 W at 60 G for sessions of about an hour, taking turns (the bowl and table never run together)
law: Sustained pedalling by an average adult about 75 W (kit limit); at 80 G the 62.8 W is near it (PR-006 at risk)

claim: Direct smelting of the table concentrate with borax recovers the gold with no mercury
law: Gold melts at 1,064 C; borax fluxes oxide and silicate gangue into a slag. Benguet miners smelt gravity concentrates with borax (Appel and Na-Oy 2012); the US EPA cites concentrates of about 50 to 100 g. A sulfide-rich (pyrite, arsenopyrite) concentrate can carry gold into a matte and fume arsenic, so it may need the sulfides removed or roasted first
check: Depends on the partner's ore; smelting is outside the machine (RSK H10)

claim: Mercury in old tailings would be concentrated by the bowl, so the machine must never process mercury-contaminated material
law: Liquid mercury (13.5 g/cm3) and amalgam are denser than quartz and report to any gravity concentrate
check: A hazard, not a performance claim: kept as a safety rule in PRC, RSK and the README

claim: The cast PU liner lasts 500 h or more on quartz feed
law: Elastomer and ceramic wear linings are used in commercial centrifugal concentrator bowls (a moulded rubber insert lasted 1.5 to 2 times the ceramic tiles at Detour Gold; Canadian Mining Journal 2014); life of this cast PU on this feed is unknown

claim: Settling ponds and flooded pits near the machine can breed mosquitoes
law: Malaria transmission is linked to mining sites, where pits and ponds hold standing water (studies of mining workers in Muara Enim, Indonesia, Scientific Reports 2023, and of a malaria outbreak at illegal gold mining sites in French Guiana)
check: A site risk: pond fencing, covering or draining with the partner (RSK H7)

claim: Heavy-mineral concentrates can carry arsenic (arsenopyrite) and lead; gloves and hand washing control the exposure at clean-up (smelter fume is the smelting step's hazard, RSK H10)
law: Arsenopyrite is a common gold-bearing sulfide; arsenic is acutely and chronically toxic (WHO arsenic fact sheet)
check: Safety rule in PRC and RSK

claim: The GFRP shell does not buckle under the full jacket's pressure with the bowl empty and the holes blocked, at 1,200 rpm
law: Windenburg-Trilling short-cylinder buckling of the 4 mm shell between the riffle rings (38 mm pitch), E = 7 GPa hand-laid GFRP, liner ignored (independent review's missing case)

claim: A full tank on the 1.7 m post does not resonate with the table drive
law: Post above the brace node as a cantilever under the 64 kg tank: about 3.5 Hz, against the table at 4.0 to 5.0 Hz and the harmonics of the bump stop impacts (independent review); with the brace node raised to 1.6 m about 7.5 Hz
check: Near resonance. Fix proposed: raise the brace node to 1.6 m (about +0.5 kg, which takes PR-011 over 100 kg) or run the table with the drum drained; to Amish (GVS-DEC-001 O3)

claim: Option B: the 12 mm diaphragm stroke lifts the water over the ragging bed by at least 5 mm each pulse
law: Displaced volume = effective diaphragm area x stroke, spread over the screen area
closed_by: GVS-OPT-001 (model: 190 mm plate in a 216 mm free opening)

claim: Option B: the pedal drives the jig with about 15 W
law: Work to lift the bed pressure over the displaced volume, twice for losses, at 240 strokes/min

claim: Option B holds free gold coarser than about 0.1 mm but loses much of the finer gold
law: Jigs are not efficient for fine gold particles and need narrow size fractions (Veiga and Gunson 2020)
check: Within known science; scored against UR-003 in OPT

claim: Option B uses about 2.3 m3/h of water (hutch water at about 6 mm/s plus slurry water)
law: Hutch upflow over the bed area plus slurry water; jigs need large amounts of water (Veiga and Gunson 2020)

claim: Option C holds gold coarser than about 0.1 mm; recovery falls below 20 % for gold finer than 100 um
law: Sluice recovery drops to less than 20 % for grains finer than 100 um (Mitchell et al. 2026); good recovery of 105 to 212 um gold with expanded metal riffles (Poling and Hamilton, UBC pilot study)
check: Within known science; scored against UR-003 in OPT

claim: Option C uses about 2 m3/h of water running at about 10 % solids
law: Water at 10 % solids by mass for 200 kg/h of solids; large sluices use far more (Veiga and Gunson 2020)

claim: Option C's concentrate (about 1 to 2 % of the feed, 15 to 30 kg per shift) is panned by hand to a smeltable 100 g
law: Sluices concentrate weakly (mean ratio 2.5 at Migori; Mitchell et al. 2026); panning tens of kilograms a day is hours of stooped work
check: Plausible on paper; the labour is scored in OPT
